text.approach: The X Couloir is most directly approached from the south via the Middle Fork Nooksack River Road (FR-38); the less direct alternative starts at Heliotrope Ridge and reaches the southwest face through the Thunder Glacier cirque. Drive FR-38 toward its mile-12.5 switchback and start hiking/bushwhacking the old decommissioned road around Pt. 4481 toward Rankin Creek — snow travel (often by bike or snowshoe on the lower stretch) leads past East Rankin Lake (~5,120 ft) and up into the basin to a sheltered camp at treeline around 6,100 ft, near the highest trees in the basin below Seward Peak. From camp, an alpine start gets the team into the southwest basin and across the bergschrund crux while it's still cold and firm, climbing roughly 1,500 ft of 30-40° snow and a steep serac step in the X Couloir to the 9,085 ft summit. Total approach is on the order of 7 miles and 3,350 ft of gain to the basin camp. Important — access note: FR-38 (Middle Fork Nooksack River Road), damaged in the December 2025 floods, has been closed to vehicles at milepost 7 by a washout since 27 July 2026, with no end date given on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026, and a separate seasonal gate at Wallace Creek (~mile 10) closes the road December 1-June 15 for elk calving; confirm current road status with the Mount Baker Ranger District (Glacier Public Service Center) before a trip, since the drivable road-end — and therefore the length of the approach — varies y

text.overview: Lincoln Peak's SW Face route, known as the 'X Couloir' (sometimes referenced as 'X Couloir – Emancipation Proclamation'), is the historic line up this seldom-climbed, seriously loose Black Buttes summit. First climbed by Fred Beckey, Wesley Grande, John Rupley, and Herb Staley on July 22, 1956, it was the only documented route to the summit until a 2015 first ascent opened a second line on the NW Face. Only about a dozen ascents are known; the peak is guarded by near-vertical walls on every side
text.descent: Most parties reverse the ascent line, downclimbing and rappelling the same southwest gully/couloir system (the X Couloir) back down into the southwest basin below the face. This is a real rappelling descent, not a walk-off: the most detailed documented descent (a repeat/'2nd descent' trip report) describes 10 double-rope rappels — 4 off pickets placed by the descending party, 1 off a sling around

lastAnswer.notes: Two equally cited starts: Heliotrope Ridge TH (Wikipedia: SW face via Thunder Glacier cirque from Heliotrope Ridge Trail; USFS 48.802236,-121.89559) and the FR-38 Middle Fork Nooksack road (route's own text calls this the direct one; Wikipedia also names it as alternate; road-end near mile-12.5 switchback unplaceable, FR-38 closed at milepost 7 since July 2026; USFS Middle Fork Nooksack TH 48.726672,-121.900293 is another candidate). Left for owner decision.

text.overview: A roughly 1,500-ft alpine rock route up Chaval's north ridge: mostly moderate 3rd/4th-class scrambling on solid, well-fractured granitic rock, with two harder pitches on the steepest section near the top.
text.descent: Parties commonly traverse off the summit and descend the West Route's ramp/heather line rather than downclimbing the North Ridge.

lastAnswer.notes: SummitPost (403) and CascadeClimbers pages unreadable. Only readable page (turns-all-year, West face) starts from the car on Illabot Road, no named lot. A 2017 SummitPost log (search summary only) says a party found the North Ridge too ambitious in a day and used the Illabot approach instead. Grade Creek spur may be undrivable. No page ties the North Ridge to a start.
